newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-SACRAMENTO RUNS PERFECT TACTICAL RACE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SACRAMENTO RUNS PERFECT TACTICAL RACE.

text.p: Portuguese Carla Sacramento ran a tactically perfect race by avoiding the bumping and grinding among the pack to win the world women's 1,500 metres title on Tuesday.
Sacramento, 25, clocked four minutes 04.24 seconds to take the gold medal easily ahead of Regina Jacobs of the United States, who was second in 4:04.63.
Anita Weyermann of Switzerland, who muscled her way into contention on the last lap, clocked 4:04.70 to edge Spain's Maite Zuniga (4:04.80) for the bronze.

Ireland's Sonia O'Sullivan, 5,000 metres champion in Gothenburg two years ago, was well placed at the bell, but was left behind in the sprint for the line in the last lap. She finished eighth in 4:07.81.
Malin Ewerlof of Sweden who led for much of the race was also buried in the rush, coming home a distant 10th in 4:08.68.
The race was an untidy, cautious and physically tough one, especially in the final 400 metres.
Sacramento, who laid down her credentials for the title when she ran the fastest mile of the year at Nice three weeks ago, stayed well clear of the rough stuff and powered home to win in some style.
